utterances.text: -- limited to any request relation to, let's say, the story of those who are -- or the absence of any story of those who are seeking asylum or relocation, that if any request is made in that respect, that even if they do not appear on the list of witnesses but to the knowledge of the Defence have been interviewed at any earlier stage by an OTP investigator or whether any interviews are disclosed to the Defence by the OTP, that notification will be given of such a request to Mr. Re so that he is in a position to express his concerns, if he has any.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just for Your Honours' re-assurance, the practice of my team - and I believe the practice of every other team - has been to address the request first to Mr. Re; in other words, we go first to the Prosecution to ask whether they have the material. And generally we get the response that it's not the Prosecution's area of responsibility. Once or twice we've had material served. But the requests are almost always made -- I think always made in the first instance to the Prosecution; that will continue to be the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, full transparency, Mr. Re, as far as it comes to the delicate issue of information about those who have been seeking asylum or relocation. Yes. May I take it that the review of the redacted statements has not been finalised yet or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I read them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the implications of them need to be considered. I can certainly see a realistic possibility in respect of one, possibly more than one, but certainly one that in due course we will be seeking to pursue the identification of the individual in order that they might be approached potentially as a witness. Now, that is not something I want to finalise at this stage; I think it needs more mature consideration. But I mention it because it could lead on to the procedural issues that I raised right at the very beginning of the hearing and that the UNMIK representatives had adverted to, namely the possibility of Your Honours hearing UNMIK on some of those issues in closed session in the absence of the parties, but at the moment it's premature. I'm simply conscious of the fact that the UNMIK representatives are here. My own practical suggestion is that we adjourn that issue for the time being and see if we can resolve it through the procedures which have now been -- the structures that have now been provisionally agreed between the parties and endorsed by the Trial Chamber. If that proves to be unworkable, then it may be necessary for there to be some process of litigation with the Trial Chamber resolving it, and I would imagine that might start at least on paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then also the Chamber would have a -- of course better material to rely upon because I take it that then the disclosed material would be made available to the Chamber as well so in order to understand why you would like to revisit the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I just so that Your Honour -- and I think Your Honour is alight to the issue in any event. It potentially could arise on the context of the cross-examination of a particular witness, and it was an issue that I raised during the cross-examination of the last witness about whether the kidney was inside or outside the body. The witness concerned is not imminent, I understand, in other words it's not a situation that needs to be resolved over the next 72 hours; but on the other hand, it's not something that could be adjourned, so to speak, till much, much later in the Prosecution case because my understanding is that the Prosecution are intending to call the witness within the foreseeable future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Borg-Olivier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BORG-OLIVIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record I just wish to confirm that, together with my colleagues, we have prepared redacted statements, three of them, and these have been provided to the Defence and the OTP because this has not been said, so I'm saying that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BORG-OLIVIER
utterances.text: And of course we stand to be guided by whatever further direction the Chamber will give us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll leave it for the time being to the parties what follow-up to give to it, and if they address the Chamber seeking invitations or orders at a later stage we will see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BORG-OLIVIER
utterances.text: Another addition in connection with Mr. Harvey's request, I mean it's not clear to UNMIK what is expected of UNMIK, but we take it it's understood that questions of asylum and relocation are highly sensitive matters. If any questions are brought to our attention, we don't make any commitment at this stage as to how we can respond. But of course in most instances these will involve the Office of the Prosecutor more than UNMIK if they are matters related to proceedings before this Chamber. But general issues of asylum we can certainly pass on to the authorities that deal with these questions and see if there's any useful information that can be passed on. To the extent that, Your Honour, you suggested that perhaps Rule 70 constraints could also be imposed on Defence, while we have of course every confidence in the professional responsibilities of the Defence, it's not quite the same to get sort of safe-guards through the Office of the Prosecution, which is a public office that is, you know, more controllable and accountable than Defence attorneys, in general. And I say this in a very general sense. But we'll see if and when we need to make any caveats, we might have to seek the Court's -- or this Chamber's assistance in how best to ensure those safe-guards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it doesn't need further explanation that the Defence is, as we find it in our rules, is counsel and accused; of course that means professionals and nonprofessionals with different interests, perhaps, in the case. Also if we compare that to the interests the Prosecution may have, again different interests and I would say just professional interest. Finally, before we finish. Mr. Guy-Smith, what to do with the 12th of January motion? You earlier asked us to -- not to decide upon that. Would that still be the case or would you withdraw it at this moment? Because whatever will happen, it certainly will not be exactly the same motion to decide upon anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that based upon the proceedings today that the motion, as it's presently constituted, is a motion that I would be willing to withdraw because in the event there is any further litigation on the issue, you're right, the motion will take a different position. I may -- hopefully I won't, but I may need to allude to those principles that are raised and some of the law that's raised in that motion in a future motion. But at this point in time, I think it would be appropriate to withdraw the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A second ago you said that you would be willing to withdraw the motion. Now the last words were that "I think it would be appropriate to withdraw the motion." Do you withdraw the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I always seem -- I always seem when speaking with you to have more than one word. The answer is: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then this is then on the record, that the motion has been withdrawn. I don't think there is any other matter, Mr. Borg-Olivier, Madam Ciaravolo, or Mr. Dalton, that needs your attendance. I'd like to thank you very much for taking the effort to come to inform the Chamber and to assist in resolving the matter that was bothering the Chamber at this moment. And the Chamber expresses confidence that future dealings with all parties will go as smoothly as they went today. I'd like to thank you very much. I also would like to have a break at this moment. After the break we'll deal with some remaining procedural matters in accordance with the -- with the agenda that has been provided to the parties. We adjourn until 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps before we -- I give you an opportunity to address the Chamber, the Chamber would very much like to be informed first of all whether our discussions on -- and perhaps we go into private session to discuss the matter. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Emmerson, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply wanted to mention one matter. Your Honours will have in front of you four schedules. They are headed respectively: Documents and photos for Haradinaj Defence; cross-examination of, and then Witness 21 – (redacted) (redacted) -- I'm sorry, I think we need a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. There's an error on that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the witnesses we find the names on the top of these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. For four of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What these are are -- essentially are the indices to the bundles that were used in cross-examination with the P numbers marked on those that have already been marked for identification, and they are shaded in grey. Anything that is not shaded in grey has not yet been marked for identification, and that is a process that will need to take place. I haven't done or I haven't handed Your Honours the same exercise in respect of Witness 8 or John Crosland because in neither case is their testimony concluded. It could be done, but my submission to Your Honours in respect of both of those two witnesses is going to be the question of the tendering and admission of exhibits for each of them should be concluded, in Mr. Crosland's case, when his testimony concludes and, in the case of Witness 8, if and when he is re-called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then suggest the following, that is that we leave the lists for the time being in the hands of Madam Registrar, that she assigns numbers to it, that we receive the lists -- at least I receive the list back, and then I'll just briefly read out in court exhibit number so-and-so-and-so and it will be that. So that it's on the record but we do not spend any further time on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think what, Madam Registrar, was most keen should be clear on the record is the linkage between tab number and the final D number so that -- so that when it goes into the record it's possible to cross-refer when I'm asking a witness about a document behind tab 6, in those instances where I haven't, as I should have done, had it marked for identification at that very moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and that cross-referencing can be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar prepares it all and we'll just read it all out in court so that it's clear. Then I just received a copy of a VWS report on Witness 29. I'll have a look at that, but first of all let's try to get the list of pending exhibits shorter than it is now. Madam Registrar has provided us with a -- I don't know whether -- no. I have -- let me just ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the parties have also received a list of MFI numbers where no decision has yet been taken. We see that there are green-marked documents where the Defence has expressed that it did not wish to tender these. And some of them are marked in yellow, and those are the ones where a translation has been replaced by a better one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. In both of those instances an official translation has been replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So let's now -- I also did understand that the Andjelkovic matter has not been finally resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think so far as we are concerned, at least, it can be finally resolved today. As far as the Haradinaj Defence is concerned, we've had the opportunity to review the proposals of the Prosecution. We have no objection or additional material that we would wish to exhibit. Simply by way of a caveat, the letter which is dated the 2nd of April from Mr. Re listing the proposals, I'm -- I understand - although I'll be corrected if I'm wrong - I understand that the 65 ter numbers given on that letter are in error, but that the marked for identification numbers given on Madam Registrar's schedule and the 65 ter numbers given there are correct; in other words, the schedule is correct but the letter is in error. That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Since we are not admitting any letters into evidence but rather documents. Any of the other Defence counsel, any problems with P1 to P6 marked for identification, as they now appear on the list provided by Madam Registrar? Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm in a similar position to that of those sentiments in -- mentioned by Mr. Emmerson. I want to make sure that with regard to the Andjelkovic notes contained in P1 at pages 2, 3, and 13 of those notes are admitted; the corresponding pages in P3 would be pages 19, 20, and 29 of the notebook itself. I had also, during my examination, requested that an exhibit number be given to volume 4, which was 65 ter number 696, in which I had -- that's at page I believe 2851 of the transcript, read out and I believe I had read it in its entirety, pages 3 and 4 of volume 4 of the Andjelkovic notebook. So with that in mind, I'm satisfied with regard to the first six exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To be quite honest, it's not entirely clear to me. You seem to be happy with 1 to 6, but you said you are in a similar position, you want to make sure that with regard to the Andjelkovic notes contained in, et cetera, et cetera, those notes are admitted. If they are part of the material as we find it on the list, it's not. So it should -- the list is incomplete. So these pages should be added and then a volume 4 should be added as well. Under those circumstances, I invite again the parties to find a final set of Andjelkovic exhibits and not here to get here a page or there a page in addition. Let's try to get an agreed set of Andjelkovic material to be admitted, because now to say we admit half of it and volume 4 should be added next week, that's exactly what we tried to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was hoping to avoid that. It's that there have been some gaps in the presentation made, but I'm sure we can settle this in a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, what about not later than next week Wednesday to provide an agreed list of Andjelkovic exhibits and add whatever pages should be covered by P1 or P3 or volume 4 to find its way somewhere in here, or an additional request for assigning a number to any additional set of documents, but that the Chamber receives an agreed list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- I thought we'd reached that point. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that seems --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- letter of the 18th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- referred to the 2nd of April and set out the proposed reordering all the exhibits. That was I think as far as the Prosecution can take it. They've been retranslated, we've reordered them, we've given the numbers they would have in the 65 ter list. I'm just not sure how far we can take it but I can certainly discuss it with Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't think it will be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sure we can resolve it by Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's resolve it by Wednesday. So that's the first batch we did not manage to get off the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very nearly off the list. May I simply mention I noticed that the column which records whether documents were admitted confidentially or under seal says no in respect of each of those. It may be, I don't know, that the Prosecution have already reviewed the notes to ensure that the names of protected witnesses don't appear, but I would be surprised if there were no names in there of protected witnesses, bearing in mind what it was that we saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- of the notebooks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course reference was made to some of these notes in later testimonies as well. Mr. Re, have you carefully checked that yet or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will review that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll also hear from you in this respect on Wednesday, not later than Wednesday. Then we have D9, D10, D11, and D13 not to be -- not to be tendered. That means that they're taken from the list. We keep the numbers open and we'll not at any later stage use those numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which requires also that they're formally withdrawn. The reason why we'd prefer to leave these numbers open, that later on the record we would at least know what document was ever discussed at this court or was presented. If we fill those numbers, then of course you get double numbers, then D9 is the original D9 and then the later D9, which might confuse. So we'd rather leave them open as documents that have been withdrawn, but they should be formally withdrawn by the Defence then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, then I formally withdraw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, might the Prosecution be heard on this particular matter because these are documents which were the subject of cross-examination - Mr. Di Fazio was the lawyer who was involved with one of those witnesses - as to whether or not they should form part of the trial record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Because even though the Defence has put them forward, the Prosecution has a submission it would like to make as to whether they should be in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Very briefly it's only this: Where a statement of a witness has been used in cross-examination and matters extracted from that statement and put to the witness, then it's fair, in the Prosecution's submission, that you should see that extract or section from the witness statement in the context of everything else that the witness has said so that you get a complete picture of how and why the witness says that. So for that reason, the -- the Prosecution suggests, submits, that you should accept the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I guess the response is -- MR. DI FAZIO: For that purpose only, for that purpose only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that the Defence would be very worried about having in evidence major portions of statements which we not even have read, where no attention was paid to it in any way, and where a specific portion of a statement has been read into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit Number D42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D42. If there are no objections against D37 -- MR. DI FAZIO: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then D37 and D42 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. There's a description error, I'm afraid. The exhibit that Your Honour's just assigned the number to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- was in fact tendered by Colonel Delic in the Milosevic case and not in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then the description should be corrected. Madam Registrar, you've got that? Then we move on. P266 and P267, any objection by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, no objection from -- for our part to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey? None of the Defence teams. Then P266, P267 are admitted into evidence. We then move on to three Defence exhibits, that's D38 up to and including D40. Any objection by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the Trial Chamber assist where they are on the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the list they are -- it's -- the list is chronological. You find them on the list we have now -- I've got in front of me, it's on the last page. That's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then we -- no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- most recent one. No objection. So therefore D38 up to and including D40 are admitted into evidence. And then the last one on my list is P268, a map marked by the witness. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Same true for the he other Defence teams. Then P268 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I ask Your Honour at this point to take another of the schedules that I handed in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which is the Rrustem Tetaj schedule. And Your Honours will see it's the shaded areas which form the majority of the documents behind the tabs in the bundle shown to Mr. Tetaj during cross-examination by the Haradinaj Defence team are P-numbered exhibits; in other words, they're documents that have already been marked for identification. Many of them, I think, documents that are part of the Bislim Zyrapi collection of documents as exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still to be decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Still to be decided upon, save that there is no dispute in respect of those ones. And -- and that leaves those that are not shaded which need to have an MFI number assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we invited, as a matter of fact, Madam Registrar to prepare that. I just made an exception --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- as far as the one witness was concerned because there was another -- we could deal with all the Defence exhibits there. So for these are not in grey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the things we'll carefully verify is whether the admission is always under seal where the circumstances require so. The parties are invited to check that on the basis of the list of Madam Registrar, and the Chamber will do the same, so in order not to make any mistake. Then in relation to exhibits, we have -- in relation to the exhibits marked for identification in relation to Witness Crosland, of course we have a long list. If, perhaps, an exchange could already be started on where most likely we'll find objections or not, that would certainly assist when finally the testimony of Mr. Crosland will be concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think there's likely to be very little area of dispute, if any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it would be possible to inform the Chamber, perhaps also the Prosecution, prior to the start of the continuation of the testimony of Mr. Crosland where we stand, then it may be easier to resolve and it may also be easier to proceed. I think, as a matter of fact, that in that respect the -- yes, the Limaj transcript was already admitted. Then one of the outstanding issues is that the Chamber will have to decide on the security situation concerning witnesses in Kosovo. I think we have now received the positions of Defence parties. The parties seem to agree that this, I would say, the third requirement, that is, there exists an unstable security situation in that territory which is particularly unfavourable to witnesses who appear before the Tribunal, whether we can accept this as an agreed position of both parties that it doesn't need any further evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's always been the Prosecution's position, and it's entirely consistent with the position we've taken throughout the pre-trial and the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber will consider whether or not we are going to accept that as a kind of an agreed circumstance. Yes. Then we have received a short report on Witness 29. I see it's dated this very morning, just before the start, and I am reading it now. I do understand perhaps we should go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very quick. Just to be assist the Court, my submission in relation of Witness 29, you'll find, Your Honour, at 3594 on the 26th of April your direct instruction to the witness which was that he should go accompanied by someone from the Victims and Witnesses Section to accompany him to any place where you keep one of these notes and to provide them to the person that accompanies you or someone assigned by Victims and Witnesses Section. So Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- will have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seems to be rather clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, who has also found the relevant section, said that I added to that: To the extent that it is within the competence of the VWS, because I was not fully aware at that moment to what extent VWS is competent to accompany people in their homes, even if they would not like to be accompanied by VWS. That's totally a different completely matter. So therefore we'll further inquire into the matter what actually happened and why the witness did the search on his own. Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And indeed how the next search is to be conducted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, that goes without saying. If there are no further procedural matters, I would like to thank the parties for their cooperative approach in resolving quite a lot of procedural matters. We adjourn until tomorrow, the 11th of May, 9.00, in Courtroom I.
